summary: On September 15, 2023, the city council unveiled an ambitious plan to make local infrastructure more sustainable. It covers bike lanes, pocket parks, upgraded recycling, solar panels, stormwater systems, electric buses, environmental education, business incentives, IoT monitoring and public forums. Rollout dates run from December 2023 to fall 2025, with named officials leading each component.
one_line: The city council's September 2023 green infrastructure plan covers bike lanes, parks, recycling, solar, stormwater, electric buses, education and monitoring through 2025.
key_facts: The city council unveiled its sustainable infrastructure initiative on September 15, 2023.
Councilwoman Elizabeth Torres spearheads the bike lane network meant to encourage non-motorized transit and reduce reliance on fossil fuels.
Pocket parks, led by environmental advocate Victor Green and volunteer botanists, are proposed to be in place by December 2023 and will seek input from local residents.

An upgraded recycling program, with clearly labeled containers and a public awareness campaign, is projected to be in full swing by April 2024; Sarah Chen is director of the city's waste management department.
Engineer Roberta Vasquez drives the solar initiative, which fits solar panels onto libraries, schools and recreation centers, with completion scheduled by the end of 2024.
Environmental engineer Marcus Lee oversees stormwater management systems using permeable pavement and rain gardens; implementation is poised to begin in June 2024.
Transit authority manager Maria Gomez announced a fleet of electric buses by January 2025, the first step toward converting the city's entire fleet.

A new environmental education program, drafted by the local board of education with environmental NGOs, will enter school curriculums citywide beginning in fall 2025; Joanna Lai is a curriculum expert.
Local businesses will get subsidized energy-efficiency retrofitting and sustainability awards; the Chamber of Commerce, led by Richard Tan, pledged support.
A city-wide IoT sensor monitoring system will track solar panel energy output and bike lane condition in real time; IT specialist Jamie Khan commented on it.
The city council scheduled public workshops and forums throughout 2024 for residents to share ideas and concerns.
